reason: The elite figures in this text are consistently portrayed unfavorably. King Zedekiah is explicitly stated to have 'done evil in the eyes of the Lord' (וַיַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה), rebelled against the king of Babylon, and faced severe consequences: his city was besieged, his sons were slain before his eyes, his eyes were blinded, and he was imprisoned in Babylon. The priests (Seraiah, Zephaniah) and military officers are captured and executed. Even Gedaliah, who is shown initially with some mercy toward the remaining people, is ultimately assassinated. The narrative structure emphasizes the downfall and defeat of the ruling class as divine judgment ('the anger of the Lord was upon Jerusalem and Judah'). The detailed account of their capture, humiliation, and destruction constitutes a decidedly unfavorable portrayal.
